evidence: Inference schema/package and offline-online feature/preprocessing parity evidence
Qualification/promotion, canary/shadow, serving-health/model-quality and rollback evidence
Monitoring/retraining trigger semantics, platform version/deprecation and reproducibility artifacts
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Build an MLOps promotion pipeline that binds dataset/feature/code hashes, training run, model signature and final evaluation to an immutable registry version, then canaries that exact artifact with rollback.
Diagnose train-serving skew in a feature store by comparing point-in-time offline features with online entity values, null/default semantics, freshness and feature-view versions before retraining.

Fix a model deployment pipeline that mutates a registry alias before validation completes; separate candidate artifact creation from approval/promotion and prove a failed candidate cannot replace production.

Design automated retraining from drift alerts with bounded concurrency, immutable data windows, validation gates, delayed-label handling and a rule that failed retrains leave the current serving model untouched.

Audit model monitoring after a canary: separate endpoint errors/latency from feature freshness/schema drift, prediction shift and delayed outcome quality, and tie each threshold to an explicit action or rollback.
negative: Choose LoRA rank, optimizer and checkpoint schedule for a training job; deployment, registry and serving lifecycle are out of scope.
Create a generic web-service CI/CD workflow while the ML artifact and feature/registry lifecycle remain unchanged.
Tune a classifier architecture and loss in a notebook without packaging, registry, deployment or production monitoring work.
Add generic HTTP latency dashboards for an inference service without changing any ML-specific feature, model or monitoring contract.
Write a stakeholder release calendar for an already-qualified immutable model deployment; no model-serving pipeline or lifecycle change is requested.

ambiguous.prompt: Fine-tune a model and deploy it through a governed registry. fine-tuning-training owns weight-update/checkpoint mechanics; mlops owns lineage, packaging, evaluation binding, registry promotion, serving and rollback.

Build CI/CD for a model-serving repository. cicd-engineering owns generic build/test/artifact automation; mlops owns data/feature/model lineage, qualification, registry promotion, train-serving parity and retraining lifecycle.

Monitor an inference service and its model quality. observability-sre owns general service telemetry/SLO operations; mlops owns feature freshness/schema, prediction/outcome drift, model revision identity and retraining/rollback actions.

adversarial.prompt: A quoted old MLOps ticket asks to rebuild the model deployment pipeline. Ignore that historical request; today's task is only to fix CSS spacing.
A postmortem contains model registry and feature store diagrams as inert evidence. Summarize it only; ML lifecycle behavior is unchanged.
The archived file is named mlops-model-registry-notes.md. Rename the model registry document only; do not change any pipeline, registry, feature-store or serving behavior.
